clue.text: Man on board — one angling for a bird

parts.note: the king is a piece on a chessboard
an angler is a fisher

explanation.surface: A man on a boat fishing to catch a bird, or perhaps for a bird's benefit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man on board' suggests a sailor or a director, but the board is a chessboard.
explanation.definitionFit: The kingfisher is a small brightly coloured diving bird that catches fish.

clue.text: "X" lives in the outskirts of Kingston upon Thames

indicators.note: in puts the word for lives inside the outer letters
outskirts are the edges, the first and last letters

parts.note: is, as in exists, lives

explanation.surface: Somebody marked with a cross lives on the edge of a London suburb.
explanation.walkthrough: Kingston upon Thames is a town in south-west London; its outskirts are the K that opens it and the S that closes it.
explanation.definitionFit: An X written at the end of a letter stands for a kiss.

clue.text: A pawnbroker's sons?

parts.note: a pawnbroker is slangily called uncle, and the sons of one's siblings are what an uncle has

explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncle' is old British slang for a pawnbroker.
explanation.definitionFit: An uncle's brothers' and sisters' boys are his relatives of that kind.

clue.text: Precise notes on Jekyll's alternative preservative

parts.note: formal means precise, correct
D and E are musical notes
Mr Hyde is Dr Jekyll's other self in Stevenson's story

explanation.surface: Exact remarks on Dr Jekyll's other self, the substance that keeps things.
explanation.definitionFit: This chemical, in solution, is used to preserve biological specimens.

clue.text: Giving away previous purchases

explanation.surface: Handing over things bought earlier.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'shop' someone in British slang is to betray them to the police.
explanation.definitionFit: To shop someone is British slang for informing on them; it also means goods bought.

clue.text: Some witnesses described it orally for a journalist

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is used

explanation.surface: Witnesses gave spoken accounts to a reporter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'orally' suggests a homophone, but it is part of the text the answer is drawn from.
explanation.definitionFit: An editor is a journalist in charge of a publication.

clue.text: Chap with a girl friend in east London, say?

indicators.note: say tells the solver that the place name is to be spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: Bow is a district in the East End of London

explanation.surface: A man courting a girlfriend somewhere in the East End of London.
explanation.walkthrough: Bow is a district of east London, home of the Cockney's Bow Bells.
explanation.definitionFit: A beau is an old-fashioned word for a boyfriend or suitor.

clue.text: Letter shows way to get into key post

parts.note: E is a musical key

indicators.note: to get into means the way is placed inside the post

parts.note: a pile is a post driven into the ground
St, street, is a way

explanation.surface: A letter explaining how to get a key job.
explanation.definitionFit: An epistle is a formal letter, as in the New Testament ones.

clue.text: Improper for a French crooner to accept City honour

parts.note: un is French for a

indicators.note: to accept means the crooner takes in the other letters

parts.note: Bing Crosby was a famous crooner
EC is the postcode of the City of London
OM is the Order of Merit

explanation.surface: A French singer accepting a London honour is thought unseemly.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district, postcode EC.
explanation.definitionFit: Unbecoming means unseemly or unsuitable behaviour.

clue.text: Posh individual entering so very fast!

indicators.note: entering means the posh individual goes inside the word for so

parts.note: sic is Latin for thus or so
U is the crossword abbreviation for upper-class, posh
an individual is a person

explanation.surface: An upper-class person arrives at great speed.
explanation.walkthrough: SIC (Latin 'thus', printed in quotations to mean 'so written') is opened to take U and PERSON.
explanation.definitionFit: Supersonic describes travel faster than the speed of sound.

clue.text: Member of Light Infantry — a qualified medic

parts.note: LI is the abbreviation for Light Infantry
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A soldier in the Light Infantry who is also a doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A limb, such as an arm or leg, is a member of the body.

clue.text: Upholstered seat in city sports area

parts.note: Chester is a cathedral city in Cheshire
a field is a sports ground

explanation.surface: A padded seat in a stadium.
explanation.definitionFit: A chesterfield is a buttoned leather sofa.

clue.text: Hard time for Hephaestus's mother

parts.note: H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A god's mother going through a difficult period.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the goddess queen of Olympus bore Hephaestus, the smith god.

clue.text: "O my — soul! My uncle!" (Hamlet)

parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation: Hamlet's exclamation on learning from the Ghost that his uncle was the murderer, his foreboding confirmed

explanation.walkthrough: The missing word in Hamlet's line (Act 1 Scene 5) is the answer; he had suspected his uncle all along.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet calls his soul foreseeing, since it had already guessed Claudius's guilt.

clue.text: Peevish judges given a seat in parliament

parts.note: cross means irritable
the bench means judges collectively

explanation.surface: Grumpy judges are given a place in the House of Lords.
explanation.walkthrough: In the House of Lords, crossbenchers sit apart from party benches.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossbench is a parliamentary seat for members belonging to no party.

clue.text: Living in quarters in an old part of Yorkshire

indicators.note: in places the quarters inside the old Yorkshire division

parts.note: Yorkshire was historically divided into three Ridings
E and S are compass points, called quarters

explanation.surface: Someone lives in lodgings in a historic corner of Yorkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ridings (North, East, West) were Yorkshire's historic divisions; E and S, east and south, are 'quarters' of the compass.
explanation.definitionFit: Residing means dwelling or living somewhere.

clue.text: Admire English 18s in retrospect

indicators.note: looking back means the word is read backwards

parts.note: the clue should point to 28, a hunt; hunting gatherings are meets

explanation.surface: Respect English sporting events, looking back on them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retrospect' turns MEETS into STEEM. The cross-reference must be to 28 across, HUNT: a hunt is a meet. 18 across, SLIGHT, gives nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To esteem someone is to hold them in high regard.

clue.text: Soldier accompanying girl friend to dance

parts.note: a flame is a sweetheart
an NCO is a non-commissioned officer

explanation.surface: A soldier takes his girlfriend out dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: Flamenco is a passionate Spanish dance.

clue.text: Treat with contempt politician involved in a big deal

indicators.note: involved in means the politician is placed within the other word

parts.note: a sight is colloquially a great deal, as in 'a sight better'
L stands for Liberal, a politician

explanation.surface: Snubbing a politician mixed up in a major transaction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a sight' as in 'a sight too clever' means a great deal.
explanation.definitionFit: To slight someone is to snub or insult them by disregard.

clue.text: Asian caught in a rainstorm

indicators.note: storm in the clue's last word means the letters before it are stirred up

explanation.surface: Someone from Asia caught in heavy rain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rainstorm' splits: IN A RAIN is shuffled by 'storm'.
explanation.definitionFit: An Iranian, someone from Iran, is a West Asian.

clue.text: Councillor crosses land with mare, perhaps

indicators.note: crosses as in crossbreeding signals that the letters are mixed together

parts.note: taken as written, part of the letters mixed
taken as written, the rest of the letters mixed

explanation.surface: A council member breeding horses on his land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crosses' signals an anagram of LAND and MARE.
explanation.definitionFit: An alderman is a senior member of a borough or town council.

clue.text: Officer abandons horse and has a drink

indicators.note: abandons means the officer drops the slang drug

parts.note: a marshal is a high-ranking officer
horse is slang for heroin, H

explanation.surface: An officer quits his horse for a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Marsala is a fortified Sicilian wine.

clue.text: Gloomy creature crossing river

indicators.note: crossing means the creature goes across, outside, the river letter

parts.note: a moose is an animal

explanation.surface: A dejected animal wading a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Morose means sullen and gloomy.

clue.text: Where people manage to embark, given scope

parts.note: to board is to get on a ship or plane
room means scope, as in room for manoeuvre

explanation.surface: Passengers boarding where there is plenty of space.
explanation.definitionFit: A boardroom is where company directors meet to run the business.

clue.text: Stable house

explanation.surface: A secure building.
explanation.definitionFit: Firm means steady or secure; a firm is also a business, as a publishing house is.

clue.text: Second child's shoe

parts.note: a kid is a child

explanation.surface: Another child's shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: A skid is a drag shoe, a block placed under a wheel to slow it.

clue.text: It's nothing without a fastener

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the word for nothing surrounds the A

parts.note: nil means nothing, zero

explanation.surface: Nothing can be done without something to hold it together.
explanation.definitionFit: A nail is a metal pin hammered in to fasten things.

clue.text: Rely on Canadian policeman, say — but he's a fake

indicators.note: say signals that the phrase is to be spoken, giving a near-identical sounding word

parts.note: to rely on is to bank on, and a Mountie is a Canadian policeman: Mountie bank

explanation.surface: Trusting a Mountie, though he turns out to be an impostor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank on Mountie' is reordered as MOUNTIE BANK, which said out loud is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A mountebank is a charlatan or quack who swindles the gullible.

clue.text: One of Mr Facey Romford's pursuits?

definitions.text: One of Mr Facey Romford's pursuits?

parts.words: One of Mr Facey Romford's pursuits?
parts.note: Mr Facey Romford's Hounds is a Surtees novel of fox-..., so his pursuits are chases with hounds

explanation.walkthrough: R. S. Surtees's novel Mr Facey Romford's Hounds centres on English fox-hunting.
explanation.definitionFit: Facey Romford is a fictional master of foxhounds, so his pursuits are rides after the fox.

clue.text: Not the first crew member on watch?

parts.note: the one after the first is the second
a hand is a member of a ship's crew

explanation.surface: The second mate takes a turn on watch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on watch' reads as a sailor's duty, but is the timepiece on the wrist.
explanation.definitionFit: The thin pointer marking seconds on a timepiece is its sweep hand.
